newsitem.title: USA: DQE seeks buyers for blocks of firm power.
newsitem.headline: DQE seeks buyers for blocks of firm power.

text.p: DQE Inc's Duquesne Light Co said Friday it is offering to sell at wholesale two blocks of firm power.

Provided Duquesne receives sufficient qualifying bids, the utility said, it commits to sell 50 megawatts for one year and at least 100 megawatts for eight years to the highest bidders on a dollar per megawatt hour basis.
Each calendar year, purchasers must take or pay for the power at a 75 percent annual capacity factor, Duquesne said.

The DQE Inc subsidiary said it is offering 50 megawatts of firm electrical capacity and energy for a term of one year, and at least 100 megawatts, but not more than 500 megawatts, for a term of eight years, both starting January 1, 1998. Bids are due June 26, 1997.

The utility said purchasers may submit bids to purchase all or part of the firm power, subject to a two megawatt minimum bid. Purchasers may vary their power schedules between 50 and 100 percent of the megawatt contract amount in any hour.

If Duquesne could not deliver the power scheduled by the purchaser through dispatch of its generation or the purchase of power from third parties, the purchaser would have the right to secure replacement power and Duquesne would reimburse the purchaser for any increased costs, the company said.

The winning bidders may use this wholesale purchase to supply customers in the wholesale market or the needs of their retail customers in Duquesne's or any other Pennsylvania utility's proposed retail access pilot programs this fall and later during the full phase-in of retail access.
